findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on missing or unreadable audit file
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, std::io::Error> and propagate with ? or map_err

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric value in audit file
findings.failure_mode: malformed input line crashes the loader instead of returning a parse error
findings.fix: use .parse::<u32>().map_err(|e| ...)? and return typed parse error through Result

findings.problem: lossy as u16 cast discards high bits without checking range
findings.failure_mode: values > 65535 silently truncate to u16 range, producing incorrect audit data with no error
findings.fix: use u32::try_into().map_err(...) or check range before casting; return typed error on overflow

findings.problem: Unchecked indexing into parts Vec via parts[0] and parts[1] with no bounds check
findings.failure_mode: a line with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields panics with index-out-of-bounds instead of returning a parse error
findings.fix: use parts.get(0) and parts.get(1) with Ok(_)? early returns, or use split_once(',') for single-split parsing

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is a hidden I/O side effect inside what should be a pure parsing step
findings.failure_mode: side effect couples logging to data parsing, prevents deterministic testing, and leaks I/O into the core logic
findings.fix: remove println! from the parser; move all logging to the imperative shell layer that calls the pure parser

findings.problem: load_audits mixes I/O (fs::read_to_string, println) with parsing logic in a single function
findings.failure_mode: cannot unit-test the parsing logic in isolation without mocking filesystem I/O; violates pure core / imperative shell boundary
findings.fix: split into a pure fn parse_records(lines: impl IntoIterator<Item=&str>) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> and a shell fn load_audits(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> that reads, logs, and delegates to parse_records

findings.problem: Record struct uses public String field with no validation; name can be empty, value is unbounded u16
findings.failure_mode: consumers cannot guarantee Record represents valid audit data; empty names or truncated values are silently allowed
findings.fix: use a private constructor or newtype: impl Record { fn new(name: String, value: u16) -> Result<Self, RecordError> { ... } } with validation

findings.problem: Collecting all split parts into Vec<String> allocates heap for what could be a single split_once
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocation per line increases memory pressure; for audit-heavy workloads this is a measurable performance defect
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',') to get (name, rest) without allocating intermediate Vec

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists to measure load_audits throughput or allocation profile
no profiler data (flamegraph, perf record) for the parsing path
no allocation evidence (e.g., `cargo +nightly binstall heaptrack` or allocator tracing) for per-line Vec allocation from .collect()
no second-ring audit command evidence (e.g., Miri for UB, Kani for arithmetic overflow on the as u16 cast)
no command evidence that the crate compiles or passes tests under current toolchain
residual_risk: static review only; no commands run. All fallible operations (file I/O, parsing, casting) are unguarded and will panic on adversarial input. No benchmarks or allocation evidence exist. The entire function is a monolithic I/O+parse mix with hidden logging. All blockers must be fixed before delivery.
